events.description: Rave incorporated in Ontario as WeMesh Inc.
events.quote: In 2013, Rave was incorporated in Ontario under the name WeMesh Inc.

events.description: Co-founder left and WeMesh rebranded as Rave
events.quote:
In early 2017, after Mr. Darvish-Kazem left the 
company, I rebranded WeMesh as Rave

events.description: Rave launched on the App Store
events.quote: From Rave’s launch on the App Store in January of 2015

events.description: COVID-19 surge in Rave usage
events.quote:
In March and April 2020, at the outset of the COVID-19 pandemic, Rave experienced a 
significant and unexpected increase in usage

events.description: Apple required apps with third-party login to implement Sign in with Apple; Rave implemented it
events.quote:
In or around 2020, Apple required applications that offered third-party login options to also 
implement SIWA

events.description: Apple announced SharePlay
events.quote: In the months leading up to Apple announcing SharePlay in June 2021

events.description: Apple removed the Rave App from the App Store citing Guideline violations
events.quote:
On September 28, 2023, after more than eight years on the App Store, Rave received a 
message through App Store Connect

events.description: Pazaratz submitted a point-by-point response within two hours
events.quote:
Within 
approximately two hours of the removal notice being delivered, I submitted a comprehensive, 
point-by-point response

events.description: Apple gave guidance that the NSFW toggle must be on the website
events.quote:
On September 29, 2023, Apple responded with specific guidance regarding not safe for 
work

events.description: Rave submitted version 6.8.3 implementing the changes
events.quote: On October 2, 2023, following the guidance from Apple, Rave submitted version 6.8.3

events.description: Rave sent urgent follow-up messages on October 6, 9, 10, 11 and 12
events.quote:
Rave sent 
multiple increasingly urgent messages on October 6, 9, 10, 11, and 12, 2023.

events.description: Apple reviewer Jenny called, sent a follow-up, and the app was reinstated that day
events.quote:
On October 13, 2023, a representative of App Store Review identified as Jenny attempted 
to contact me by telephone

events.description: Rave identified users attempting to share CSAM in early 2024
events.quote: Beginning in early 2024, Rave identified attempts by users to share CSAM on the platform.

events.description: Rave developed its internal CSAM detection model
events.quote:
By March 29, 2024, Rave had developed an internal neural-network-based CSAM 
detection model.

events.description: CSAM detection system deployed into production
events.quote: The system was deployed into production on April 8, 2024.

events.description: Apple warned Rave of a Guideline 1.1.4 violation
events.quote: On November 13, 2024, Apple issued a warning to Rave through App Store Connect

events.description: Apple rejected version 7.0.8 citing Guideline 1.2
events.quote:
On November 
27, 2024, Apple rejected that submission

events.description: Apple approved version 7.0.9
events.quote: On December 9, 2024, twelve days later, Apple approved version 7.0.9

events.description: Rave acquired the a-eye.com domain
events.quote:
a domain which Rave 
acquired on January 16, 2025

events.description: Apple approved version 7.0.10
events.quote:
Apple subsequently approved another update, version 7.0.10, on 
January 22, 2025.

events.description: Apple scheduled a call to discuss review of the app
events.quote:
On February 6, 2025, Apple sent a message to Rave through App Store Connect scheduling 
a call

events.description: Dylan of App Store Review phoned Pazaratz about CSAM reports and found none
events.quote:
On February 7, 2025, a representative of Apple’s App Store Review team named Dylan 
contacted me by telephone.

events.description: Pazaratz summarized the call in a Slack message to the team
events.quote:
Immediately following the call, I summarized the interaction in a Slack message to the 
Rave team.

events.description: Dylan sent a message citing Guidelines 1.1.4, 1.2 and 5.2.3
events.quote:
Later that day, Dylan sent a message referencing App Review Guidelines 1.1.4, 1.2, and 
5.2.3.

events.description: Rave sent Apple its CSAM prevention and detection document
events.quote:
Later the same day, Rave provided Apple with a detailed PDF document describing its 
CSAM prevention and detection framework.

events.description: Apple Ads strategist Nikia Harris contacted Rave
events.quote:
In or about July 2025, Nikia Harris, a Client Strategist for Apple Ads, initiated contact with 
Rave

events.description: Before the notice Rave found and fixed a technical error affecting moderation of new accounts
events.quote:
Prior to Apple issuing the August 13, 2025, notice, Rave had independently identified and 
fixed a minor technical error

events.description: Apple sent a Pending Termination Notice and removed Rave's apps from the App Store
events.quote:
On August 13, 2025, Rave received a message from Apple with the subject line “Pending 
Termination Notice”.

events.description: Rave appealed the same day
events.quote:
On the same day, Rave immediately appealed the decision through Apple’s prescribed 
process

events.description: Pazaratz tried unsuccessfully to reach known Apple contacts
events.quote:
I attempted to reach out to contacts I knew at Apple through previous projects related 
to Rave, though these efforts were unsuccessful.

events.description: Apple's first response rejecting the appeal (10:29 a.m.)
events.quote:
On August 21, 2025, eight days after the Rave App had been removed from the App Store, 
Apple responded to Rave’s appeal

events.description: Apple's second response at 1:04 p.m. adding a Guideline 1.1.4 allegation
events.quote:
On August 21, 2025, at approximately 1:04 p.m., less than three hours after Apple’s appeal 
rejection, Apple issued a second response

events.description: Rave conducted a comprehensive internal investigation
events.quote: Rave immediately conducted a comprehensive internal investigation.

events.description: Rave responded to Apple disclosing the technical error and seeking reinstatement
events.quote:
On August 25, 2025, immediately after Rave concluded its internal review, Rave responded 
to Apple.

events.description: Apple sent a status update that the appeal was being evaluated
events.quote: On August 30, 2025, five days after Rave submitted its August 25, 2025, response

events.description: Apple advised the membership would be terminated
events.quote: On September 3, 2025, Apple issued a further response through App Store Connect

events.description: Two meetings with Apple Ads strategists about an approximately $1 million engagement
events.quote:
This outreach led to two consecutive meetings held 
on September 4, 2025

events.description: Ms. Riles followed up saying Apple conducts a thorough investigation
events.quote: On September 12, 2025, Ms. Riles followed up again

events.description: Rave retained counsel; Sam Stake wrote to the App Review Board
events.quote: On September 15, 2025, given the seriousness of the matter

events.description: Apple's counsel Tony Bedel responded asking for more time
events.quote: On September 17, 2025, Tony Bedel, a lawyer at Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP, responded

events.description: Stake replied asking for a timeline
events.quote: On September 18, 2025, Mr. Stake replied

events.description: Stake followed up on progress
events.quote: On September 24, 2025, having received no further update, Mr. Stake followed up again

events.description: Google Play sent Rave a CSAM policy violation notice
events.quote:
On September 24, 2025, Rave received a CSAM policy violation notice through the Google 
Play Console

events.description: Bedel said an update would come by the end of the following week
events.quote: On September 25, 2025, Mr. Bedel said that he did not have a substantive update

events.description: Owen Roberts filed the Google appeal, acknowledged the same day
events.quote: Owen Roberts filed an appeal on September 26, 2025

events.description: Roberts sent Google a substantive response attaching the Illegal Content Detection document
events.quote: On October 1, 2025, Roberts sent a substantive response

events.description: Stake wrote again about the eight-week removal
events.quote:
On October 7, 2025, 
Mr. Stake wrote again

events.description: Bedel said the request would be evaluated by the App Review Board
events.quote: On October 9, 2025, Mr. Bedel responded

events.description: Stake asked for a decision by October 24
events.quote: On October 20, 2025, Mr. Stake again wrote to Mr. Bedel

events.description: Apple issued a further rejection after re-evaluation, adding CSAM, bestiality and 5.2.3 allegations
events.quote: On October 22, 2025, Apple issued a further rejection notice through App Store Connect.

events.description: Rave's counsel requested a direct conversation and proposed an in-person meeting
events.quote: On October 24, 2025, following receipt of Apple’s October 22, 2025, rejection notice

events.description: Bedel replied that Apple stood by termination and declined to meet
events.quote: On October 30, 2025, Mr. Bedel replied

events.description: Rave sent a final written communication to the App Review Board
events.quote:
On November 3, 2025, after Apple declined to meet or engage further, Rave sent a final 
written communication

events.description: Apple closed the matter through App Store Connect
events.quote: On December 18, 2025, Apple sent a message to Rave through App Store Connect.

events.description: Apple sent a formal notice terminating the DPLA and ADA
events.quote:
On December 19, 2025, the day following the December 18 App Store Connect message, 
Rave received a formal notice of termination

events.description: Apple revoked Rave's Developer ID Certificate, causing macOS malware warnings
events.quote:
On December 19, 2025, in connection with the termination of Rave’s Developer Program 
membership, Apple also revoked Rave’s Developer ID Certificate.

events.description: Apple invalidated Sign in with Apple credentials and push notification tokens
events.quote:
At the same time as the termination of Rave’s Developer Account on December 19, 2025, 
Apple invalidated the Sign in with Apple

events.description: After removal Rave received many user complaints
events.quote:
Following removal from the App Store, Rave experienced a significant volume of user 
communications

events.description: Google closed the appeal and approved the resubmitted app
events.quote:
On February 3, 2026, Google Play representative Vesta closed 
the September 2025 appeal

events.description: West Virginia Attorney General sued Apple over iCloud CSAM
events.quote:
On February 19, 2026, West Virginia Attorney General John B. "JB" McCuskey filed a 
consumer protection lawsuit

events.description: Kansas Attorney General issued a release and letter to Apple on iCloud and CSAM
events.quote: On March 20, 2026, Kansas Attorney General Kris Kobach issued a press release

events.description: Rave's iOS and overall users and revenue declined

iOS monthly active users declined from approximately 2.78 million users in July 2025 to 
approximately 461,707 in April 2026
